summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 3, part 122), a helicopter flies low through a storm over jungle, searching for a place to land. The narrator spots a clearing and the pilots set down, only to find a large paved plaza beneath the trees, dominated by a brand-new-looking stepped pyramid in the Mayan style. The narrator remarks that the site resembles 'Jungle Disneyland,' and notes that Army personnel are present, hinting at a secretive operation. The passage ends with the helicopter landed and the pilot Villatoro staring at the pyramid.
one_line: A storm-battered helicopter lands in a jungle clearing beside an unexpected, brand-new Mayan-style pyramid guarded by Army personnel.
key_facts: The narrator is flying in a helicopter over jungle during heavy rain, searching for a clearing where the storm can be waited out.
The narrator spots an opening in the trees and Alan orders Villatoro to bank back and go look at it.
The helicopter descends toward the clearing, and the treetops are described as parting like the Red Sea as it settles.
A man-made hill topped by a stone building is visible in the glare of the landing lights.
The structure is described as a stepped pyramid in the classic Mayan style that looks brand new.
The pyramid stands over one side of a large paved plaza that is mostly hidden from the sky by overhanging trees.
The rotor wash throws spray off the paving stones, which glisten under the landing lights.
Alan remarks that the whole place is 'Jungle Disneyland' and that the operation is not about Mickey Mouse.
Alan says there is plenty of Army presence hanging out around the site.
Lieutenant Villatoro is described as an ex-Army pilot who guides the chopper's descent.
The helicopter's skids thump onto the stones and the passengers fall silent.
At the end of the excerpt, Villatoro keeps glancing over at the pyramid.
